Subject: [Urgent] Production errors during heavy concurrency burst

Hi Grace,

We observed a sharp spike in 429/503 errors on our Redwood Dedicated pool starting ~08:45 PDT this morning during a scheduled marketing push. Latency jumped from ~50ms to 800-1200ms and several requests returned 503. We've attached a small bundle with client-side traces and a transcript of a failing request (runway-prod-logs-20270830.zip).

Impact:
- ~12% of inference requests within our peak window failed or timed out (reported by our metrics)
- Several downstream workflows retried and caused backlog in SQS

We are on a tight timeline for a client demo tomorrow and need immediate remediation steps and an ETA for full recovery. Please advise root cause and whether this is related to our Dedicated capacity config or a broader Redwood issue.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera

Thanks Alex/Grace — brief technical summary and actions taken so far.

Observation (initial):
- The Dedicated autoscaler evaluated active sessions using a heuristic that undercounts long-lived streaming connections when KV-prefix cache hits are above 90% for a pool.
- During the marketing push, a small subset of RunwayAI clients created many short, high-parallel inference sessions that bypassed prefix cache warm paths. This produced a pathological scheduling state where the autoscaler did not scale out quickly enough and existing nodes experienced queue pileup.

Immediate mitigations applied (10:00–10:20 PDT):
1) Hotfix deployed to polling logic to correct active-session accounting (autoscaler-hotfix.patch attached).
2) Temporary +20% headroom provisioned on RunwayAI's Dedicated pool (manual reserved nodes added).
3) Tenant-level admission control enabled to cap per-tenant concurrent inflight requests to a safe threshold while the hotfix rolls out.

Status: Traffic now shows median latency back down to ~120–180ms and 503s reduced to <0.5% in the last 15 minutes. We will keep admission control in place until we observe 48 hours of stable behavior or complete the autoscaler fix to mainline.

Next steps (itemized):
- Follow-up rollout: full autoscaler fix to canary → regional → global (target: 48h). Jira: RI-9845.
- Postmortem draft by Wed 2027-09-01 with timeline, root cause, and long-term architectural mitigations (KV cache instrumentation, autoscaler stress tests).
- Proposed customer compensation: 10% credit for the impacted billing period (Ben to confirm commercial).

Logs and artifacts: see attached logs and the internal ticket link: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/RI-9845

If anyone on the RunwayAI side sees residual errors, please paste a sample request id and timestamp.

—Rishi
